chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no sin except that a believing servant has it imprinted upon him; he avoids it for a time, then commits it.
Those who avoid the great sins and immoralities, except for minor slips.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Lammam is the servant who commits a sin after a sin, which is not from his nature, i.e., not from his inherent disposition.'

key_terms.يُلِمُّ: To commit or touch upon (a sin)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Lamam in the Quran and how does it relate to the nature of a believer's sins?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies that 'Lamam' refers to occasional, non-habitual sins committed by pious believers, distinguishing them from those whose nature is inherently sinful. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that such lapses do not negate one's faith, provided the sin is not a permanent characteristic of the individual's disposition.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin isa, from Hareyz, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is none from a sin except that it gets imprinted upon a Momin servant, fleeing from it for a time, then committing it,
and these are the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [53:32] Those who keep aloof from the great sins and the immoralities except for the ‘Lamam’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Al-Lamam is the servant who commits the sin after the sin, it not being from his normal tendency, i.e., from his nature’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from (Hariz) from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Any sin that may become imprinted in a believing servant (of Allah) he shuns it for a period of time then commits it again
as it is mentioned in the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘ . . . those who avoid the major sins and the indecent acts except the al-Lamam . . .’ [53:33]
The Imam said, ‘One committing al-Lamam, sins often, is he (servant) who commits such sins one after the other and it is not of his normal behavior and nature.’”
